newsitem.title: UK: Feb demand lifts NWE heating oil premiums.
newsitem.headline: Feb demand lifts NWE heating oil premiums.

text.p: NWE gas oil demand for Feburary delivery lifted cargo premiums on Thursday but barges remained lethargic on warmer weather and buyer reluctance, traders said.
"The Feburary numbers are picking up. There is more buying interest because people have got their Feburary buying programmes together," a cargo trader said.
Benchmark Feb futures gained $4 to $207 a tonne at 12.45 GMT on fairly bullish U.S. crude and distillate stocks data.
French quality heating oil cargoes were bid at Feb +$11 for prompt cif Le Havre, around unchanged, but February 1-15 delivery was bid at 6.50 cif Bordeaux, around $2 firmer.
German winter grade heating oil for Feburary 1-15 delivery was bid $2 stronger at Feb IPE +$6.50 cif NWE. Prompt was bid a touch higher at Feb IPE +$9.50 and offered at +$11 cif NWE.

Russian heating oil was put at Feb IPE +$5/7 for prompt, around unchanged. A French major is still seeking a 20,000 tonne cargo of low sulphur diesel, apparently bidding at Feb +$20/21, the level of its purchase on Wednesday.
Barges were lethargic. Refinery grade heating oil was offered at Feb IPE +$6/5.50 and bid at Feb IPE +$4.50/5. February 1-15 delivery was around +$2/3.50 fob ARA.
